subject: Another question about annotate(), how to change text units?

messages.author: ae61b6b8911d6ad3
messages.subject: Another question about annotate(), how to change text units?
parts:
Like :

library(ggplot2)

width = 0.5
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = factor(cyl), y = mpg, fill = factor(cyl))) +
    geom_bar(stat = "summary",
             stat_params = list(fun.y = mean),
             geom_params = list(width = width, color = "black")) +
    geom_errorbar(stat = "summary",
                  stat_params = list(fun.y = mean,
                      fun.ymax = function(x) mean(x) + sd(x),
                      fun.ymin = function(x) mean(x) - sd(x)),
                  geom_params = list(width = width * 0.8, color = "black")) +
    coord_cartesian(ylim=c(0,50)) +
    annotate('text',2,40,label='P = 0.03')  #####All i want is its size to be the same as axis text

Best regards,
Meng Zhao

2013-9-18

messages.author: 373beb702917b8b5
messages.subject: Re: Another question about annotate(), how to change text units?
parts:
I don't believe there is a way to change the text size units. Getting
the text label to be the same size as the axis label is hard because
a) the axis text is not a fixed size, but rather relative to the
base_size, and b) the axis.text size is in pts while the label size is
in mm. The best I can come up with at the moment is

annotate('text',2,40,label='P = 0.03', size =
(theme_gray()$text$size * theme_gray()$axis.text$size)*.35)

but this is not only ugly, it's also fragile.

Best,
Ista
